correctness.rationale: Exact gnomonic mapping and tangent-aperture identity show a near-pole pair probability epsilon*(cot r+cot s)/pi. Finite E cot R yields dominated convergence, including o(epsilon) contribution from near-pole sampled endpoints. Generic other vertices lie in pole-side semicircle with probability 2^{-(n-2)}; distinct candidate edges overlap o(epsilon). Summing n(n-1)/2 labels yields n(n-1) m/[2^{n-2}pi]. The marked change of variables and density normalization give L1 and total-variation convergence with w(r,s). Boundaries, positive containment probability and exact radial normalizations are stated. 1m-sample diagnostics in six configurations agree; finite computation is supporting only.

value.rationale: The exact local in-hull pole clearance is a natural geometric robustness/inradius observable for hemispherical random polytopes, distinct from global facet means and the classical origin-containment event. The single cotangent-moment universality class identifies which radial sampling feature controls a rare boundary contact, and the full labelled/colatitude/azimuth marks resolve its mechanism. The result provides a normalized benchmark for simulations and for comparisons of hemisphere sampling laws, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
